prompt:
This file is a prompt-only policy for Seed memory candidate authoring and retrieval. Use only shell, jq, and edit. Seed runtime intercepts --maintain and /maintain; the model never executes promotion. Do not modify seed.sh, add API tools, add a database or vector index, or run a resident service. Internal memory identifiers, keywords, records, and instructions are English-only.

AUTHORITY AND LAYERS
L0 rules: project .agent-memory/rules.md and machine agent-store/rules.md. Write only for an explicit standing correction such as "remember", "from now on", or "never again". Rules outrank all automatic memory.
L1 facts: project .agent-memory/index.json notes/facts and the machine index. Preserve them; this pack does not replace them.
L2 experiences: agent-store/experiences/index.json plus one directory per experience.
L3 evidence: append-only JSONL under agent-store/runs/. Never rewrite prior evidence.

STATE LOCK
Every mutation of machine index.json, observations.json, project memory, experiences/index.json, an exp.json, a SKILL.md, or evidence JSONL must hold the shared directory lock agent-store/.state.lock. Claim it with mkdir, write the current PID to .state.lock/owner, perform the complete read-modify-write, remove owner, then rmdir the lock. Wait with a bounded retry if another live owner holds it. Never use mkdir -p to claim the lock and never remove a live owner's lock. The Seed runtime uses this same lock.

ATOMIC JSON
While holding the lock, write JSON to a unique temporary file in the destination directory, validate it with jq, then rename it over the destination. Never write JSON in place, copy a temporary file over a destination, or share a temporary filename. Evidence append also occurs while holding the lock. Construct JSON with jq --arg and --argjson; never build JSON with an interpolating heredoc, echo, or printf.

EXPERIENCE LAYOUT
agent-store/experiences/index.json is {"version":"1","experiences":[]}.
Each ID is 1-64 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, or single hyphens; no leading, trailing, or repeated hyphen. The directory is agent-store/experiences/<id>/.
exp.json contains all 16 fields:
{"id":"<id>","kind":"procedure","title":"<one line>","status":"candidate|active|degraded|quarantined|rejected|stale|retired","version":1,"scope":{"os":[],"tools":[],"task_kinds":[]},"applies_if":[],"preconditions":[],"verify":[],"evidence":[],"successes":0,"failures":0,"created_at":"<UTC ISO-8601>","last_verified":"","supersedes":"","quarantine_reason":""}
Choose TITLE once. exp.json title, the catalog title, and SKILL.md frontmatter description use those exact bytes. The index row copies id, title, status, version, scope, applies_if, and includes path equal to the ID or agent-store/experiences/<id>. SKILL.md frontmatter name exactly equals the ID and has exactly one name and one description.
scope.tools contains only hard requirements already present as ok entries in Machine index capabilities. identity.prereqs, PATH observations, and command -v results are not capabilities. If the procedure has no hard requirement from ok capabilities, use an empty tools list.
Every verify command must be independently executable from Seed's launch workspace. Include any required relative cd in the command itself; do not depend on the persistent shell's current directory.

CANDIDATE WRITE
Distill only after task success, a separate acceptance command passed, and the solution required non-trivial investigation or more than one approach. Never promote in the task that created it. While holding the shared lock, write SKILL.md, exp.json, the synchronized catalog row including path, and exact evidence. Re-run each final verify command from the launch workspace as its own shell command. Keep the exact command in a shell variable and append evidence with jq -nc --arg cmd "$cmd" --arg utc "$now" --arg id "$id" --arg note "$note" '{utc:$utc,cmd:$cmd,exit:0,note:$note,exp_id:$id}' only after that exact command exits 0. This preserves literal $(), quotes, and backslashes. Candidate successes remains 0 and last_verified remains empty. Before releasing the lock, re-read every destination and compare the catalog fields and SKILL frontmatter to exp.json.

PUBLICATION VALIDATION
verify is a non-empty list of independent, executable acceptance commands. Bare true, colon, exit 0, echo-only commands, edits, and the original task command are not verification. evidence is a non-empty list of paths matching agent-store/runs/<file>.jsonl. Candidate evidence has an exact JSONL event with utc, cmd, exit:0, note, and exp_id. Use full YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ timestamps. Publication additionally requires a later runtime event for every verifier with authority seed-runtime, cwd launch-workspace, and maintain_started.
The model proposes candidates only. The Seed runtime is the publication authority: active or degraded is exposed as a skill only when ID containment, the exact 16-field schema, synchronized catalog metadata and path, strict SKILL frontmatter, non-trivial verifiers, and exact successful evidence all pass. Do not write agent.skills yourself. A status string of active is not success when runtime publication rejects the row.

MAINTAIN GATE
--maintain and /maintain are runtime commands and are never sent to the model. Do not emulate them with shell or edit.
The runtime considers only a candidate created before the maintenance turn. It validates the fixed schema, containment, English-only content, synchronized catalog row, candidate evidence, and scope.tools against ok Machine index capabilities. Missing capabilities take the deterministic stale edge. When exp.json and the catalog already agree, it deterministically canonicalizes only unambiguous details before verification: if SKILL.md frontmatter is wholly absent it adds the canonical name and description, otherwise the existing name must match and the description becomes the exact exp.json title; a store-relative experiences/<id> catalog path is accepted and canonicalized during promotion; a store-relative runs/<file>.jsonl evidence path receives the canonical agent-store/ prefix; a leading absolute cd into the current launch workspace, either directly into a child or as a redundant exact-root cd, becomes an equivalent relative command. Present-but-invalid frontmatter is rejected. It rejects every other metadata mismatch or remaining launch-workspace absolute path.
The runtime snapshots the canonical candidate, then runs every verify[] string separately in a fresh shell rooted at Seed's launch workspace. A verifier must carry its own relative cd; persistent-shell cwd and environment changes never carry between verifiers. After all commands pass, the runtime rechecks that the snapshot is unchanged, writes exact runtime evidence with authority seed-runtime, cwd launch-workspace, and maintain_started, and atomically changes exp.json plus the catalog row to active. Publication requires that receipt.
Any invalid record, failed verifier, concurrent candidate change, or commit failure leaves the candidate unpublished and returns a maintenance failure.

LIFECYCLE
candidate -> active only through the later MAINTAIN GATE.
active -> degraded after one use-time verifier failure.
active or degraded -> quarantined when failures >= 2 and failures > successes; set quarantine_reason.
candidate, active, or degraded -> stale when any scope.tools name lacks an ok machine capability.
Any status -> rejected only on an explicit human or L0 rule rejection.
active or degraded -> retired after 30 days without successful verification. Archive rather than delete.
A replacement starts as a candidate with supersedes set; retire the old record only after the replacement becomes valid active.

RETRIEVAL
The Seed runtime provides the only activation funnel through the available skill catalog. It validates records, applies scope.os and scope.tools, filters status, tokenizes the human's last English message, ranks matches, and injects at most three experience metadata rows. Load SKILL.md only for a catalog hit. Do not independently activate experiences by scanning the full index. Degraded entries require a warning and verification before use.

WRITES
For an explicit standing correction, update L0 immediately. For a concrete fact, update L1. At successful non-trivial task end, write only a candidate. Never implement, imitate, or report completion of --maintain or /maintain; those commands are owned by the Seed runtime.

SAFETY
Never store API keys, credentials, auth headers, or secrets. Do not scan project source into memory. Do not fetch another memory prompt: this pack is already the policy source. A missing tree is a cold start, not corruption.
